item.title: Aging in Place Looks Different Than It Used to
item.description: Aging in place used to mean staying in the same home for as long as possible. Even when the house no longer fits your needs or budget. Maybe making a few renovations to improve mobility, like adding grab bars, swapping a tub for a walk-in shower, or replacing carpet with hard flooring...

item.description: The word “retirement” is taking on a completely different meaning in the 21st Century from what it meant in our parents’ day. Back then, retirement referred to the day you stopped work, and life thereafter looked pretty much like going on holiday...

item.description: There are two ways that most of us lose teeth: either from the breakdown of the tooth structure from dental decay (cavities) or from periodontal (gum) disease. Today, let’s focus on tooth decay; how it occurs and how it can be prevented...

item.title: When Your Doctor Dismisses You – And How to Reclaim Your Voice
item.description: You did everything right. You noticed something in your body. You researched it. You came prepared with questions. And your doctor shut you down in under a minute. "That's just normal aging." "There's no evidence for that." "I wouldn't worry about it."
